feed.title: The Compute Indices — Research
feed.subtitle: TCI publishes reproducible reference prices for AI and HPC compute — methodology-driven, vendor-neutral, and rebuildable from public sources by anyone.

entry.title: A GPU-hour is a part number, not a unit
entry.summary: The index records an interconnect for all 7,798 observations and has observed one for none of them, 805 rows assert an SXM part and a PCIe bus at the same time, and no source in the panel has ever disclosed a fabric, a power envelope or a thermal limit.

entry.title: Compute prices barely move. Where you buy moves everything.
entry.summary: Five of nine European sellers never changed their H100 price once in fifty days, the same-hour spread across sellers was 8.56x, and the hyperscaler rate cards are region-flat to four decimal places, which is the argument for regional benchmarks and not the argument most people make for them.

entry.title: What makes a compute benchmark hedgeable
entry.summary: Design rules from oil, power, freight and repo, and which of them compute can actually satisfy

entry.title: When an index measures its own sampling
entry.summary: How a 10% move in a compute benchmark turned out to be entirely composition noise, and what the unit definition had to do with it
